text:
alex: Heads up — deploy-bot aborted the publish of web-proxy to gcr in us-central. Push returned 409 with 'manifest checksum mismatch' and deploy-bot fell back to previously pinned digest. Noticed during the midday release window. Anyone available?

priya: Ugh, saw that once when our registry mirroring re-wrote the layer order. Did the build produce multiple manifests (arm/amd) and mirror collapsed them?

alex: CI artifact shows multi-arch manifestlist created. Local digest expected: sha256:9f8e7d... but GCR reflected sha256:1a2b3c... The deploy log indicates mirror rewrite for regional replica.

deploy-bot: publish attempt blocked repo=redwood/web-proxy tag=release-2026-03-21 reason=checksum-mismatch fallback_digest=sha256:1a2b3c4 logs:
```
2026-03-21T20:02:11Z deploy-bot: put-image manifest_digest=sha256:9f8e7d... -> HTTP 409 CHECKSUM_MISMATCH
2026-03-21T20:02:11Z registry-mirror: resolved to regional_digest=sha256:1a2b3c... (from replica)
2026-03-21T20:02:12Z deploy-bot: selecting existing digest=sha256:1a2b3c4 for tag release-2026-03-21
```

raj: If we let the tag point at the wrong digest that's bad. We should either fail publish or pin to previous stable and open a rollback ticket. Does the unattested digest have attestation?

emily: quick check — attestation for sha256:1a2b3c4 is present but it's for an older build (build-5201). The new manifest sha256:9f8e7d has attestation in CI but didn't replicate to GCR yet.

priya: Action plan: 1) revert tag to stable digest (sha256:ab00ff) for prod traffic 2) coordinate with registry team to re-sync attestation for sha256:9f8e7d to regional mirror 3) republish exact manifest to GCR with unique tag release-2026-03-21-republish and attach attestation.

alex: Agreed. I'm going to pin prod to sha256:ab00ff and open a rollback PR for the release notes. Doing it now.

deploy-bot: ACTION: rollback pin applied to prod at 3412343250 by alex. Current prod tag release -> sha256:ab00ff. Canary remains 0%

emily: I'll file a support ticket with the registry mirror team and include the manifest payloads + cosign attestations. Tagging infra-mirror.

raj: Also add a pipeline check: if registry returns a different digest than expected, fail the publish (don't fallback). We keep seeing silent fallbacks.

priya: I'll put up a hotfix PR to the publish pipeline to require "manifest_digest == registry_selected_digest" and to require attestation on selected digest. Test included.

alex: For republish, use this snippet (gcr):
```bash
# republish the exact manifest to the regional registry
gcloud artifacts docker images add-tag gcr.io/redwood/web-proxy@sha256:9f8e7d... gcr.io/redwood/web-proxy:release-2026-03-21-republish --verbosity=info
# attach cosign attestation
cosign attach attestation --key $COSIGN_KEY gcr.io/redwood/web-proxy:release-2026-03-21-republish --predicate-file attestation.json
```

emily: Filed ticket MIRROR-482 with registry team, included logs and CI attestation. Assigned to @infra-mirror.

deploy-bot: Update: rollback pin verified at 3412343400. Republish required (manual).

raj: Once republished and attested, we should run a checksum verify job that pulls the manifest from GCR and compares SHA to CI expected before flipping canary.

priya: I'll wire the verify job into deploy pipeline as a gating step. ETA for PR ~2 hours.

alex: Customer-release notified and release window marked with a partial rollback note. Adding this thread to the release notes and to postmortem draft.

emily: Mirror team responded: investigating replication lag and manifestlist normalization. They expect a fix in ~45m and will force re-sync.

priya: OK — if mirror fix happens quickly we'll republish and run the verify job, then resume canary to 5% -> 25% steps. If not, we'll keep prod pinned and delay full release.

alex: Thanks all. Postmortem action items: 1) forbid silent fallback on checksum mismatch; 2) add republish+attestation flow docs; 3) create monitor for registry replication lag. I'll open followups.
